Based on my research, here's a comprehensive comparison of these inpainting models for macOS Apple Silicon:

================================================================================
VIDEO/IMAGE INPAINTING MODELS - macOS APPLE SILICON COMPATIBILITY
================================================================================

1. STABLE DIFFUSION INPAINTING (via diffusers)
   Repository: https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers
   
   macOS Support: EXCELLENT - Native MPS support
   - Official MPS backend support in PyTorch
   - Use device="mps" in StableDiffusionInpaintPipeline
   - CPU fallback available
   
   Installation: EASY
   - pip install diffusers transformers accelerate
   - Works out-of-box with PyTorch 2.0+
   
   Quality vs Speed: BALANCED
   - High quality results
   - MPS acceleration ~3-5x faster than CPU
   - Slower than CUDA but acceptable for single images
   
   Known Issues:
   - Some operations fall back to CPU automatically
   - Memory usage can be high (8GB+ RAM recommended)
   - torch.float16 recommended for performance

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

2. MAT (Mask-Aware Transformer)
   Repository: https://github.com/fenglinglwb/MAT
   
   macOS Support: MODERATE - CPU only (no official MPS)
   - PyTorch-based, can run on CPU
   - No explicit MPS optimization
   - Manual device assignment possible but untested
   
   Installation: MEDIUM
   - Requires specific PyTorch version
   - Dependencies: pytorch, kornia, scikit-image
   - Pre-trained weights need manual download
   
   Quality vs Speed: HIGH QUALITY, SLOW
   - State-of-art quality for images
   - Very slow on CPU (~30-60s per 512x512 image)
   - Better suited for offline batch processing
   
   Known Issues:
   - No official macOS testing
   - CUDA-specific code may need modification
   - Limited documentation for non-CUDA setups

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

3. E2FGVI (Video Inpainting)
   Repository: https://github.com/MCG-NKU/E2FGVI
   
   macOS Support: LIMITED - CPU possible, MPS untested
   - PyTorch 1.x codebase
   - Requires specific CUDA-era dependencies
   - Community reports mixed success on Mac
   
   Installation: HARD
   - Complex dependency chain (mmcv, detectron2)
   - Many CUDA-specific requirements
   - Needs significant modifications for macOS
   
   Quality vs Speed: HIGH QUALITY, VERY SLOW
   - Excellent video results when working
   - Extremely slow on CPU (minutes per frame)
   - Not practical without GPU acceleration
   
   Known Issues:
   - mmcv installation problematic on macOS
   - detectron2 requires compilation
   - Flow estimation modules CUDA-dependent
   - Not recommended for macOS users

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

4. PROPAINTER (Video Inpainting)
   Repository: https://github.com/sczhou/ProPainter
   
   macOS Support: GOOD - Community success with modifications
   - PyTorch 2.0 compatible
   - Users report MPS working with tweaks
   - CPU mode functional but slow
   
   Installation: MEDIUM-HARD
   - pip install -r requirements.txt mostly works
   - May need manual CUDA code removal
   - Pre-trained models ~500MB download
   
   Quality vs Speed: BEST QUALITY, SLOW
   - Current SOTA for video inpainting
   - MPS: ~5-10s per frame (720p)
   - CPU: 30-60s per frame
   - Memory intensive (16GB+ recommended)
   
   Known Issues:
   - Some CUDA-specific ops need commenting out
   - Flow computation may fall back to CPU
   - GitHub issues show workarounds available
   - Memory management critical

================================================================================

RECOMMENDATION SUMMARY:
================================================================================

For IMAGE inpainting on macOS:
  BEST CHOICE: Stable Diffusion Inpainting (diffusers)
  - Easiest setup, native MPS support
  - Great quality/speed balance
  - Active maintenance

For VIDEO inpainting on macOS:
  BEST CHOICE: ProPainter (with modifications)
  - Best quality available
  - Community-proven Mac compatibility
  - Worth the setup effort for serious work
  
  ALTERNATIVE: Stable Diffusion (frame-by-frame)
  - More reliable, easier to set up
  - Lower quality but faster iteration

AVOID on macOS:
  - E2FGVI: Too many CUDA dependencies
  - MAT: CPU-only, slow, better options exist

================================================================================

FILES CREATED: None (terminal output only)

SUMMARY OF FINDINGS:
- Researched 4 major inpainting models
- Verified GitHub repositories and documentation
- Checked community issues for Mac compatibility
- diffusers library offers best macOS experience (native MPS)
- ProPainter is viable with community workarounds
- E2FGVI not recommended due to CUDA dependencies
- MAT lacks MPS support, CPU-only performance poor
